name: mbrd-desktop
description: The Electron shell. A second package rather than dependencies on the root one, which declares none and must keep declaring none - `npm test` at the root installs nothing and CI's first leg is what checks that claim. electron-updater, sharp and onnxruntime-node are runtime dependencies of this app and could not live there. Note the absence of "type": "module": both bundles are CommonJS because a preload script under sandbox:true must be, and one format for the package is cheaper than two rules. The version is 0.0.0 on purpose - the release workflow reads VERSION out of web/assets/js/version.js and stamps it here, so there is one stamp rather than three, and an unpackaged run has no version at all (which is why the updater refuses to run unless app.isPackaged). The build marks every runtime dependency external rather than bundling it: sharp and onnxruntime-node carry .node binaries esbuild cannot inline, and electron-updater has to be resolvable from the packaged node_modules for electron-builder to wire its metadata. They are `dependencies` for exactly that reason - electron-builder ships those and prunes the rest. `productName` is here and not only in electron-builder.yml because they are read by different things: electron-builder's names the executable and the installer, and this one is what `app.getName()` answers, which is what `app.getPath('userData')` is built from. Without it the name falls through to `name` above and a person's boards live in `%APPDATA%/mbrd-desktop` - the package's name rather than the app's. Changing it after a release would strand every board written under the old path, so it is settled here before there is one.
